cli.title: Oba CLI
cli.description: Work with Kazan from your terminal with the oba CLI: tickets, comments, daily updates and the PR channel. Releases support macOS and Linux on amd64 and arm64.

install.title: Install
install.homebrew: With Homebrew, from the Korur tap:
install.script: With the installer: it picks the archive for your system, checks its SHA-256 checksum and installs oba in /usr/local/bin when that is writable, else in ~/.local/bin. It never calls sudo.
install.userInstall: OBA_INSTALL_DIR chooses another directory. Add the directory to your PATH when the installer says it is missing.
install.direct: By hand: download oba-cli_<version>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz from the latest release, compare its SHA-256 digest with oba-cli_<version>_checksums.txt, and put the oba binary from the archive on your PATH.

signIn.title: Sign in
signIn.description: oba login opens your browser and signs you in with your Oba account. Then choose the organization the commands act in and check who you are signed in as.
signIn.org: Without oba org use, commands act in the default organization of your account. --org <name|id> runs one command in another organization and keeps the chosen one.

board.title: Choose a board
board.description: Make one board the default board of the current organization. Each organization keeps its own default. Without an argument, oba kazan board use lists the boards and lets you pick one.
board.override: --board <name|prefix|id> runs one command on another board. A ticket key such as OPS-42 names its own board.

everyday.title: Everyday commands
everyday.description: A short set to start with.

items.mine: List the tickets assigned to you on every board you are a member of.
items.get: Show every field of a ticket.
items.create: Create a ticket on the default board. Title, type, priority, status and mission rank are required.
items.update: Change the status of a ticket; every other field keeps its value.
items.comment: Add a comment to a ticket.
items.updates: Write and post your daily update. On a terminal it starts from your tickets in progress and shows a preview before posting.
items.pr: Share a pull request in your organization's PR channel.

everyday.help: oba kazan --help lists every command, and oba kazan <command> --help shows its flags.

json.title: Output for scripts and agents
json.description: With --json, stdout holds only the data the API returned, as JSON; tables, messages and prompts go to stderr. A failed command prints no JSON: its exit status (2 for not found, 3 for forbidden, 1 otherwise) and the error on stderr tell why.
